overview: This Senate resolution designates February 2025 as "American Heart Month" to raise awareness of cardiovascular disease, meaning heart disease and stroke. Its opening section notes that cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in the United States and lists major risk factors such as high blood pressure, high cholesterol, poor diet, tobacco use, physical inactivity, obesity, and diabetes. The resolution supports promoting awareness, supporting research, and improving outcomes for people with heart disease, and encourages everyone to learn their own risk. Presidents have proclaimed February as American Heart Month every year since 1964. The resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or funding; the Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on February 21, 2025.
for: Supporters say heart disease kills more Americans than any other cause and much of the risk can be reduced, so raising awareness and encouraging people to learn their risk can save lives.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending, and supporting research in words does not provide any new resources for it.
